evidence.detail: apply_rules_to_decks sets rule_archetype_name = 'Bad rules' whenever len(archetypes) > 1, with no ancestor-descendant check
doubled_decks() uses `HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT archetype_id) > 1` with no ancestor-descendant filter, so a deck matching both Aggro and Mono-Red Aggro is flagged as doubled
No commits add archetype_closure logic to rule.py; the ancestor-descendant check is not implemented

triage.notes: Fix requires: (1) in apply_rules_to_decks, after fetching multiple matched archetypes, query archetype_closure to remove any archetype that is an ancestor of another matched archetype, then re-evaluate whether the remaining set is size 1 or still ambiguous; (2) similarly filter doubled_decks SQL or its post-processing. Both functions in rule.py need changes and the logic must correctly handle chains of depth > 1.
